newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 10.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 10.

text.p: All crude ports reopened and Tabasco state port Frontera remained closed Tuesday as of 1000 local/1600 GMT, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.
Dos Bocas reopened on 1730 local/2330 GMT Monday as wind speeds relaxed, port capitan Jorge Rojano Rodriguez said.
Crude port Pajaritos in Veracruz state reopened Monday 0800 local/1400 GMT after being closed most of the weekend.
The ministry reported Frontera port closed amid southeast wind speeds of 30 to 40 kilometers per hour.
Smaller boats were restricted from sailing at the following ports because of wind speeds: Salina Cruz, Puerto Madero, Ensenada and Rosarito.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Light rains along the coast of Baja California and Sonora. Winds from the east and northeast of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kilometers/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves as high as three to five feet.
Winds in the Gulf of Tehuantepec heading north and northeast reached 10 to 20 knots (19 to 37 kilometers/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves nine to 12 feet high.

A cold front in the north of the gulf sending rains and winds from the south and southeast of 10 to 15 knots and wave heights of between four and six feet in the states of Veracruz, Tabasco and the Yucatan peninsula.
Tropical winds from the northeast of 10 to 15 knots carrying light rains along coast of Quintana Roo and causing waves seven to nine feet high.
